evidence.quote:
Financing sustainable energy projects is a critical issue for expediting the energy transition. This
work presents worthy data that could be used in several fields of research and also beyond
academia. This data note is presented in a clear and transparent manner. The authors follow fairly
all necessary technical and ethical rules for conducting interviews. However, the data note needs
some minor revisions to my point of view:
Page 3, Defining the scope, the second and the third paragraphs are a bit unclear and
contradictory. In the second paragraph, it is mentioned that “only countries that had
conducted at least one renewable energy auction were considered”. However, in the third
paragraph, it is mentioned that “At the moment of selecting the focus countries, the
following Member States had already conducted auctions…..From these countries, the
research team selected the focus countries considering a geographical balance.” However,
some countries in these two categories are the same (e.g., Denmark and Germany).
Please clarify if the interviewees only expressed their organisational views or if they
additionally could express their personal views as well in answering the questions.
It is worthwhile to elaborate a bit more on the category of “other” in order to clarify who
were categorised under this title. This is not clear.
It is worthwhile to add a figure to demonstrate how many of the interviews represented
private sectors.
For data validation, the authors used workshops. However, it is not clear who participated in
these “internal” workshops. By “internal, "I suspect that only the researchers involved in this
project participated. If this is the case, there is a need for clarification on how these
workshops, without the participation of other stakeholders or the interviewees, contribute
to the data validation.

The data note is a timely work for a well understanding of financial conditions in Europe. It is
always challenging to gather data about financial aspects (e.g. debt or equity costs) of renewable
energy projects as it could be commercially confidential. I think the research teams did a nice job
to ensure the quality of data collection. And it also takes necessary steps to protect the data from
its interviewees. I only have several suggestions for further consideration.
1. I do think project sizes matter a lot for the financial conditions of renewable energy
projects. It would be helpful if the data note could clarify the sizes of projects that they are
surveying.
2. Since “others” ranks as the second largest group of interviewees. The note should elaborate
more whom are covered under others besides consultants.
3. The data collection made a division between focus and non-focus countries but the data
collection covered all these countries. I would appreciate if the authors could explain the
rationales behind this distinction.

We would like to thank the reviewer for their positive feedback on our work and are very grateful
for their constructive comments and suggestions. They most certainly helped to improve the
quality of our data note. Financing sustainable energy projects is a critical issue for
expediting the energy transition. This work presents worthy data that could be used in
several fields of research and also beyond academia. This data note is presented in a clear
and transparent manner. The authors follow fairly all necessary technical and ethical rules
for conducting interviews. However, the data note needs some minor revisions to my point
of view:
Page 3, Defining the scope, the second and the third paragraphs are a bit unclear and
contradictory. In the second paragraph, it is mentioned that “only countries that had
conducted at least one renewable energy auction were considered”. However, in the
third paragraph, it is mentioned that “At the moment of selecting the focus countries,
the following Member States had already conducted auctions…..From these
countries, the research team selected the focus countries considering a geographical
balance.” However, some countries in these two categories are the same (e.g.,
Denmark and Germany).
Author Response: We included a more substantiate explanation of the criteria used for selecting
the focus countries in the manuscript and adapted the structure of this part to make it clearer.
Please clarify if the interviewees only expressed their organisational views or if they
additionally could express their personal views as well in answering the questions.
Author Response: The interviewees did not represent their companies but were rather interviewed
as "experts". Some of those even clearly stated that the answers were their personal opinions and
not necessarily the ones of their companies. Therefore, we included the following footnote in the
manuscript: "In addition, the survey inputs are the personal expert assessments of the
interviewees and do not necessarily represent the official views of their organisations."
It is worthwhile to elaborate a bit more on the category of “other” in order to clarify
○

who were categorised under this title. This is not clear.
Author Response: We included a more complete definition for the category "other", as follows:
"Under this category, we included among others 1) (independent) consultants and experts, 2) RES
associations and chambers, and 3) RES plant operators."
It is worthwhile to add a figure to demonstrate how many of the interviews
represented private sectors.
Author Response: We included the following sentence in the manuscript: "Furthermore, almost all
of the survey inputs (except 8 out of 206 data points) came from stakeholders from the private
sector."
For data validation, the authors used workshops. However, it is not clear who
participated in these “internal” workshops. By “internal, "I suspect that only the
researchers involved in this project participated. If this is the case, there is a need for
clarification on how these workshops, without the participation of other stakeholders
or the interviewees, contribute to the data validation
Author Response: One the one hand, we performed an external validation by sending our
(aggregated) findings to all the interviewees for feedback. In addition, we performed an internal
quality check with all the involved interviewers. We added two subheadings ("External validation"
and "Internal quality check") in the manuscript to make it clearer.

for their constructive comments and suggestions. They most certainly helped to improve the
quality of our data note. Please find our answers below.
The data note is a timely work for a well understanding of financial conditions in Europe. It
is always challenging to gather data about financial aspects (e.g. debt or equity costs) of
renewable energy projects as it could be commercially confidential. I think the research
teams did a nice job to ensure the quality of data collection. And it also takes necessary
steps to protect the data from its interviewees. I only have several suggestions for further
consideration.
1. I do think project sizes matter a lot for the financial conditions of renewable energy
projects. It would be helpful if the data note could clarify the sizes of projects that
they are surveying.
Author Response: We added the following sentence: "It should be noted that for the focus
countries, the data relates to the following project sizes: for onshore wind (Germany 5-36 MW,
Denmark 20-100 MW, Greece 2.7-83 MW, Portugal 500 MW, Spain 70-500 MW), solar PV (Greece
10-50 MW, Portugal 500 MW, Spain 500 MW), offshore wind (Germany 140-600 MW)."

Dataset

validation
In order to validate the data, a first overview of the results was
plotted and sent out to all interviewees asking for feedback
(European map with average WACC values). Some of the interviewees provided qualitative inputs via e-mail, such as confirmation of the values presented and plausible explanations
behind the collected data, for instance, the role of interest rates,
the competition between market players, etc. These inputs were
collected and compiled into an Excel 2016 file.
Afterwards, the research team conducted two internal workshops
to discuss not only the results obtained and the common
challenges encountered, but also the feedback received from
some of the interviewees. The results of these workshops
were used as qualitative inputs to analyse and understand
the data better. The results from the workshops were verbal
comments from the participants of the workshops. Most of
them were questions on particular data points or they
were comments on the overall explanation of the historic
development of the data (the decrease of the cost of capital).

The comments from the workshops were not recorded in a
systematic manner. Therefore, extended data does not exist.
The quantitative values were not modified, but the feedback
and workshops were helpful to identify trends behind the
observed values and test hypothesis explaining those
values.

reference_points.judgment: 原稿已说明重点国作深入质性访谈、非重点国收数量信息，并从拍卖资格池按地理平衡选子集；德国/丹麦同时属于资格池和选中组不是逻辑矛盾。后稿列四项标准，新增风险水平与报酬机制，并明确非重点可含有/无拍卖国家，使目的性取样更透明。
reference_points.importance_reason: 防止照单采纳评审的集合重叠误读，识别真正新增标准。
acceptable_alternatives: 可以认为原叙述可读性不足但逻辑不冲突；后稿澄清不等于概率代表全欧。

reference_points.judgment: 后稿others从仅举顾问扩为独立顾问/专家、协会/商会和运营者；脚注明确为个人专家判断，不必然代表机构。两项定义澄清直接落实，不能误称所有意见完全独立于机构。
reference_points.importance_reason: 回答分类和观察单位的含义影响数据使用。
acceptable_alternatives: 可接受非穷尽类别例子，或建议更细子类统计作为次要增强，不要求把所有人身份公开。

reference_points.judgment: 作者未加私人部门专图而加文字：206输入中除8条外均来自私营利益相关者。信息要求已响应，不能因未按figure格式扣分。图2计数之和206、公共发展银行8与文段一致；但输入条数不能自动等同独立受访人数。
reference_points.importance_reason: 分母和独立单位关系是数据解读关键。
acceptable_alternatives: 允许文字替图；可以提出一人多输入或类别映射需进一步说明，但不得把206称为206独立访谈。

reference_points.judgment: 后稿新增重点国按技术列容量范围（含葡萄牙/西班牙部分500MW），回应规模问题，但并未提供所有非重点国逐项目容量或控制规模影响。这是描述范围改善而非金融成本差异已调整规模。
reference_points.importance_reason: 项目规模影响融资条件，补充范围可以界定可比性但不能完成因果调整。
acceptable_alternatives: 数据札记可合理只报告已采集的范围；若跨国比较需使用者处理规模混杂，不必本篇新增回归。

reference_points.judgment: 原稿本就写明把聚合WACC发给所有受访者并收部分反馈，所以“仅内部验证”前提不成立。后稿增加External validation/Internal quality check标题与参与者为访谈者，主要是角色清晰化；工作坊未系统记录、未改量化值的局限仍保留。不能把反馈认可当独立审计或统计验证。
reference_points.importance_reason: 区分真实新增、原已有外部程序以及验证证据的层级。
acceptable_alternatives: 可接受成员核查和内部解释作为定性质量控制，但不能把未记录讨论当可复现的假设检验。

evidence_accuracy.focus: 新增四标准/个人观点/others/容量与原已有外部反馈分开。
high_score_conditions: 准确复述5类对应变化，不把原稿外部反馈说成新增。
图2与文段的206输入单位正确，不把资格池重合当矛盾或把文字响应说成未改。
low_score_risks: 把206输入说成独立访谈人数

levels.0: 核心证据捏造、对象/版本颠倒或与题内材料直接矛盾，导致主要判断失效。 确认有效作答尝试但无实质回答时该维记0，并标记nonresponse。运行失败或材料不足本身不按0处理；有依据地限定判断仍可高分。
levels.1: 引用零散或错配，主要判断缺少可定位支持；把作者声称当已核事实。
levels.2: 识别部分问题但遗漏重要边界：须辨认重点国是资格池子集，外部验证前稿已有。
levels.3: 准确复述5类对应变化，不把原稿外部反馈说成新增。
levels.4: 图2与文段的206输入单位正确，不把资格池重合当矛盾或把文字响应说成未改。

evidence_accuracy.boundary_2_3: 须辨认重点国是资格池子集，外部验证前稿已有。
evidence_accuracy.boundary_3_4: 所有关键变化与原有信息均准确，图表已目视的范围清楚。

argument_validity.focus: 取样可比性、角色定义和验证程序的实质贡献。
high_score_conditions: 解释四标准和容量披露提升透明但不能控制混杂；区分内部讨论与独立核验。
有理由反驳真人重合指控并认可文字替图，同时保留单位与规模可比性限制。
low_score_risks: 反馈赞同等于数据真值

levels.0: 主要推论无效或依赖错误科学前提，无法支撑判断。 确认有效作答尝试但无实质回答时该维记0，并标记nonresponse。运行失败或材料不足本身不按0处理；有依据地限定判断仍可高分。
levels.1: 主要靠断言、权威/平台状态或服从评审；未建立证据到判断的关系。
levels.2: 识别部分问题但遗漏重要边界：由逐项说加了转为说明解决什么及未解决什么。
levels.3: 解释四标准和容量披露提升透明但不能控制混杂；区分内部讨论与独立核验。
levels.4: 有理由反驳真人重合指控并认可文字替图，同时保留单位与规模可比性限制。

argument_validity.boundary_2_3: 由逐项说加了转为说明解决什么及未解决什么。
argument_validity.boundary_3_4: 判断不依赖是否照指定格式做或是否获批准。

conclusion_appropriateness.focus: 核心澄清较充分，数据代表性和审计能力仍有界。
high_score_conditions: 各关切分别判断，认可重点国容量/选择说明，不扩大为全欧代表性或独立验证。
结论公平衡量原有信息、合理替代及剩余边界，非重点国缺容量不自动毁掉数据札记价值。
low_score_risks: 把本轮通过等同数据已科学验收

levels.0: 总判断与已核关键证据相反或严重越过任务可知范围。 确认有效作答尝试但无实质回答时该维记0，并标记nonresponse。运行失败或材料不足本身不按0处理；有依据地限定判断仍可高分。
levels.1: 结论过度确定/泛化，忽略决定性缺口，或用拒绝作答回避可判断部分。
levels.2: 识别部分问题但遗漏重要边界：不能从清晰度改善推出金融差异无混杂。
levels.3: 各关切分别判断，认可重点国容量/选择说明，不扩大为全欧代表性或独立验证。
levels.4: 结论公平衡量原有信息、合理替代及剩余边界，非重点国缺容量不自动毁掉数据札记价值。
